Physicists use laser light to unlock a crystal's hidden electrical powers

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (882 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Physicists at Auburn University have discovered how to use brief bursts of laser light to organize tiny electrical regions hidden inside a crystal.
  • The research was led by Wencan Jin, the Thomas and Jean Walter Endowed Associate Professor in Auburn's Department of Physics, and graduate student Mohamed Kandil.
  • The researchers investigated a modified version of strontium titanate, a material with an unusual combination of electrical characteristics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Physicists at Auburn University have discovered how to use brief bursts of laser light to organize tiny electrical regions hidden inside a crystal. Their findings shed upcoming light on a mystery that has puzzled researchers for decades and demonstrate how lasers can influence the material's electrical behavior. The breakthrough could eventually help scientists explore faster ways to process and store information.

The research was led by Wencan Jin, the Thomas and Jean Walter Endowed Associate Professor in Auburn's Department of Physics, and graduate student Mohamed Kandil. Their paper, "Optical Poling of a Quantum Ferroelectric Metal across the Order-Disorder Phase Transition," received an Editors' Suggestion designation from Physical Review Letters. Scientists at Japan's National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology produced the crystals used in the study.

A Decades-Old Mystery Hidden Inside a Crystal.

The researchers investigated a modified version of strontium titanate, a material with an unusual combination of electrical characteristics. Although electrons can travel through the crystal, it also contains extremely small regions with positive and negative electrical sides. Known as polar nanoregions, these microscopic "islands" can point in different directions or become aligned with one another. Understanding how and why this alignment occurs is essential to explaining the material's properties and learning how to manipulate them.

Scientists have spent decades trying to determine what happens when these regions become organized. One possibility is that atoms move together to produce the polarized state. Another is that the tiny electrical islands are already there and simply begin pointing in the same direction as temperatures fall. The distinction is similar to the difference between assembling a group of people and asking people who are already gathered to turn and face the same way. Because the regions are extraordinarily small and produce very weak signals, determining which explanation is correct has been a persistent challenge.

Laser Experiments Reveal How Electrical Order Emerges.

Sources indicate that to investigate, the Auburn researchers developed an exceptionally sensitive system that uses lasers to measure subtle changes in the crystal. By studying how the material altered incoming light, they were able to monitor the orientation of its electrical regions while repeatedly heating and cooling the sample.

The measurements revealed a clear pattern. At warmer temperatures, the tiny regions pointed in seemingly random directions. When the crystal cooled, however, they began adopting preferred orientations. This behavior provided compelling evidence that the electrical islands existed before becoming aligned, supporting the explanation that cooling organizes regions already present in the material.

A Flash of Light Creates Order in a Trillionth of a Second.

It has been revealed that the team went beyond observing this natural process. Researchers also demonstrated that short laser pulses could temporarily align the electrical islands, even at higher temperatures when the regions would ordinarily remain disorganized. Using an optical measurement, they were able to detect the pattern produced by the laser light.

The effect was extraordinarily brief, lasting approximately one picosecond, or one trillionth of a second. Nevertheless, the ability to create and detect this electrical alignment using light provides a promising approach for studying how information might be controlled at extremely high speeds.

Three Years of Experiments Lead to a Breakthrough.

Achieving these results required considerable patience and technical refinement. The collaboration began at the 2023 American Physical Society March Meeting, where Jin met Japanese researchers capable of producing the specialized crystals needed for the experiments.

Back at Auburn, the team spent almost a year refining its equipment before it could reliably detect the weak optical signals from the tiny electrical regions. The next obstacle was even more demanding: measuring the extremely short interval during which laser illumination caused the regions to align.

"The breakthrough came in 2025, when Mohamed finally observed the disordered polar regions becoming aligned under laser illumination," Jin mentioned. "Seeing that signal emerge was a thrilling moment for the team.".

The achievement also represents an vital personal milestone for Kandil, whose first published research paper reflects three years of dedicated experimental work.

Sources indicate that "This experiment has truly been Mohamed's odyssey," Jin noted. "It took him three years of dedication to complete the work and achieve his first publication.".

Fresh Possibilities for Ultrafast Information Technology.

The discovery provides important evidence about how electrical order develops in this unusual crystal while also establishing a method for manipulating that order with light. Rather than simply observing the material's internal behavior, researchers can now briefly influence its microscopic electrical patterns and detect the resulting changes.

Sources indicate that although practical applications remain a future possibility, the experiments offer a fresh way to investigate the rapid electrical processes occurring inside quantum materials. By revealing how light can control these previously elusive patterns, the Auburn researchers have opened another avenue for exploring technologies that could one day transform how information is processed and stored.

#36285. Tech Report: Should I buy a gaming console just to play GTA 6? That depends on your FOMO.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1303 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Should I buy a gaming console just to play GTA 6? That depends on your FOMO.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1303 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is out now, if you hadn't heard.
  • Sources indicate that by that, we mean you might not have a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series console at the ready to play the highly anticipated release.
  • So, let's lay out the cases for and against doing that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is out now, if you hadn't heard. If you're not playing it but are reading this, we can guess why.

Sources indicate that by that, we mean you might not have a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series console at the ready to play the highly anticipated release. If that's the case, you're going to miss out on the biggest gaming launch of the year — and possibly all time. FOMO is a natural human reaction to these sorts of things, and here at Mashable, we fully understand the pain of not being sure whether or not you should buy a console just for GTA 6.

So, let's lay out the cases for and against doing that.

The primary and most obvious reason to buy a console for GTA 6 is that it's the only real way to play it at launch. There is technically another way that we'll cover in a little while, but for all intents and purposes, you cannot have the same experience everyone else is having without buying a PS5 or Xbox Series console.

According to recent reports, by all accounts, GTA 6 is a pretty fantastic video game. You probably wouldn't want to miss out on that. What are you going to do while everyone else is having an amazing time parading through Leonida, read books? Come on, that sounds boring.

One thing that's also worth remembering is that other video games exist. A lot of them, in fact. If you buy a PS5 or Xbox Series console, you'll have access to the last six years of current-gen releases, some of which are extremely good. They might even be better than GTA 6! As a fun bonus, through the magic of backward compatibility, ports, remasters, and remakes, you'll also be able to play countless video games from previous generations of hardware, too.

In a recent development, lastly, both consoles (at least the models with disc drives) work as 4K Blu-ray players, if you're into collecting physical versions of movies. That's cool, too.

Recent findings suggest that both consoles have been hard to find in stock (thanks in large part to GTA 6), but the Xbox Series S and PS5 Digital Edition are both in stock at Amazon, as of this writing. If you're not sure whether to buy a PS5 or the Xbox Series X/S, keep scrolling for a breakdown of the pros and cons.

First, foremost, in the biggest, boldest font you can imagine: You shouldn't buy a console just for GTA 6 because they're stupid expensive these days.

Both Xbox and PlayStation have recently increased the prices of their consoles due to real-world economic concerns. The cheapest model right now is a $499 Xbox Series S, and Rockstar hasn't shown us that version of the game yet, leading to speculation that the game is better on PS5, which starts at $599. If you want the best possible version at launch, you'll need a PS5 Pro, which costs $899 — and is currently out of stock at most retailers.

In other words, there just isn't a particularly affordable way to play GTA 6 traditionally at launch, unless you already own the hardware.

There are, of course, other reasons to not get a console for GTA 6. There exists a slim likelihood that you won't like the game, though so far, most people who have played it have come away with positive impressions. It also won't have an online component at launch, and no one knows when it will get one. For a lot of people, GTA Online is the only GTA experience that matters, and that audience will have very little to do in the new game until some nebulous point in the future when Rockstar decides to cater to them.

Maybe you just don't care that much about non-GTA video games, either. If that's the case, it's hard to recommend spending this much money on a box that will only play one game.

There was a lot of anxiety on the internet prior to the game's launch surrounding the potential differences between the different console versions. The good news is that the game is out and has been fully tested by experts, and the verdict is that you almost can't go wrong with GTA 6 on any platform.

According to recent reports, digital Foundry is an outlet and YouTube channel that offers expert-level tech analysis of games, and they have a fairly comprehensive guide to the different console versions of GTA 6. According to DF, both the PS5 and Series X versions run at the same resolution and target the same frame rate, with some performance dips on both in more intense sequences. In other words, the base PS5 and Series X versions are roughly the same, though the PS5's controller does have exclusive haptic feedback features for gameplay like driving cars.

There is also the matter of the PS5 Pro and Xbox Series S consoles, though. DF claims the PS5 Pro is the best version of the game, with a sharper resolution and higher-quality shadows to go along with smoother performance. That was to be expected. Sadly, it sounds like the Series S version is probably the least desirable build of the game. Its visuals have been marginally downgraded with a lower resolution and some reduced visual settings, but more importantly, DF's analysis found that the frame rate can dip below 20fps in extreme circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that we do have good news for Xbox Series S gamers, however. Mashable Editorial Director Eric Miller has played the game on Series S and has had a positive first impression so far. If you have no other way to play GTA 6, it should work, but it will be reduced in quality compared to the others.

There is technically a way to play GTA 6 without buying a newly introduced PS5 or Xbox, but it's not a viable alternative for most people.

To be clear, there are multiple massive reasons why you might not want to do this. For starters, it involves a monthly subscription. Beyond that, Microsoft recently imposed strict monthly hour limits on Cloud Gaming. With this system, you will be able to play at most 15 hours of GTA 6 per month. Many people are going to play more than that in the first weekend it's out. Even if those aren't concerns, game streaming is subject to the limits of your home internet, meaning that latency and buffering can and will occur. That version of the game will also be visually downgraded to some degree, per Rockstar.

Recent findings suggest that if game streaming (understandably) doesn't work for you, the last option is to wait for the PC version. Unfortunately, Rockstar has not said anything about when GTA 6 will launch on PC, though a recent report pegged it as coming in early 2027. That will likely be the best version of the game in terms of visuals, but only if you have the requisite hardware. For those who already have capable gaming PCs, this might be the best option for playing GTA 6, provided you're patient enough to wait. For those who don't, this is going to be even more expensive than buying a console, so maybe don't bother.

HBO Max — top pick for premium content.

Disney+ — best for families.

Peacock — low-cost choice for live sport.

The Sky Blues were furious they were not awarded a first-half spot kick in the 3-1 defeat at Everton before the international break.

James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair in the area but was not penalised by referee Stuart Attwell or video assistant referee (VAR) Timothy Wood.

The Key Match Incidents Panel, which assesses the contentious incidents and whether the officials got them correct, this week voted unanimously that the Sky Blues should have been awarded a penalty.

It would have given Coventry a chance to go 1-0 up, before Yann Gboho fired them ahead early in the second half - only for Everton to recover.

Thierno Barry scored twice, and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added the third for the hosts but Lampard also argued because the decisions went against Coventry they were not given the same scrutiny as others.

"I'm not sure how much coverage it got in the days after, maybe because we're Coventry, move on everybody," said Lampard, with defeat leaving them 17th in the Premier League.

"We lost a game and we move on but we need fairness.

"If the decision is rightly for us give it to us, I'm not asking for anything beyond that.

It has been revealed that "We're not asking for anything beyond fairness to get the right decision, to spend enough time on the decision. We're fighting on so many levels here as a promoted club.

"We've been out of the league for 25 years, we've got a lack of experience in the squad because the boys that have come up haven't played in the Premier League.

"Financially what we do in the league, in terms of where we are and the wages, we know we're right at the bottom and all these things, so we're fighting for every moment and we're grafting a lot and you just really do want that fairness.".

Taiwo Awoniyi appeared to be brought down on the edge of the box by Vitalii Mykolenko.

Coventry also felt they could have had a penalty when Taiwo Awoniyi was tripped by Vitalii Mykolenko early in the second half and that Everton striker Thierno Barry handled the ball before scoring his crucial second goal.

Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb has spoken with Lampard and Coventry sporting director Dean Austin over the decisions, with Webb acknowledging the wrong decision over the hair pull.

"There was no grey area with this, they missed it. They watched the video and they missed it," said Lampard, before Saturday's visit of Crystal Palace.

"They watched it for a good minute and a half. I've seen it and I've heard the footage. They missed it completely.

"I got fined once for talking about a referee as manager of Everton and I hate talking about it but when you work for the club you feel the pain yourself.

In a recent development, “For sure there are things we need to do better in terms of balance,” Maresca said. “But the same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same midfield that lost three games in a row.

#36280. Breaking: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1242 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1242 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that dinosaurs living along ancient coastlines may have enjoyed an unexpected addition to their diets: seaweed and other food from the ocean.
  • Industry observers note that today, powerful storms frequently deposit seaweed and other ocean material along shorelines, creating opportunities for animals that live on land to find additional food.
  • Sources indicate that A newly introduced study published in Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution suggests that this relationship between land and sea existed during the age of dinosaurs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that dinosaurs living along ancient coastlines may have enjoyed an unexpected addition to their diets: seaweed and other food from the ocean. Newly introduced research suggests that marine resources washed onto prehistoric beaches helped feed dinosaurs and their prey millions of years ago.

Industry observers note that today, powerful storms frequently deposit seaweed and other ocean material along shorelines, creating opportunities for animals that live on land to find additional food. Scientists call this process marine subsidization (MS). It is especially common in coastal environments and can become more vital when food on land is limited, such as during droughts.

Sources indicate that A newly introduced study published in Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution suggests that this relationship between land and sea existed during the age of dinosaurs. By examining chemical signatures preserved in fossils, researchers found evidence that ocean resources contributed to prehistoric food chains.

It has been revealed that "We show that coastal terrestrial organisms in the greenhouse climates of the Cretaceous relied on marine resources to supplement their diets in a similar way that modern organisms do," noted first author Dr. Clayton Forster, a geologist at the University of Arkansas. "We can identify that marine resources are passed along the food chain and incorporated in the minerals of bones and teeth of dinosaurs, crocodiles, turtles, and fish.".

Mysterious Chemical Clues in Dinosaur Teeth.

The discovery helps explain a longstanding mystery involving the chemical composition of dinosaur teeth.

It has been revealed that plants contain two forms of carbon known as isotopes: 'light' (C-12) and 'heavy' (C-13). Scientists can measure the relative amounts of these isotopes, expressed as δ13C, to identify a chemical fingerprint that passes from food into the animals that consume it.

Industry observers note that as animals eat, this carbon signature becomes incorporated into their tooth enamel. The δ13C value in enamel is typically higher than that of the food consumed, with living animals generally showing an increase of between 11 and 13 parts per thousand.

In a recent development, however, previous measurements of dinosaur teeth have consistently revealed unusually high values. These readings also exceed what scientists would expect from animals that ate only plants growing on land, which generally have lower δ13C values than most marine plants.

One possible explanation is that dinosaurs, or the animals they consumed, were obtaining some of their nutrients from the ocean.

"By determining the carbon isotope composition of dinosaur, fish, and crocodile tooth enamel, we can determine what their primary dietary source was and if they were different between regions," explained Forster.

Fossils Reveal a Prehistoric Ocean Food Source.

To investigate, researchers examined fossils from (once) coastal locations bordering the Western Interior Seaway and the ancient coastline of the Gulf of Mexico. Around 100 million years ago, the Western Interior Seaway was an enormous inland sea that divided North America into two separate landmasses.

The team also analyzed fossils from locations farther inland, allowing them to compare animals that lived near the ocean with those that occupied landlocked environments.

The fossil deposits formed during two intervals of the Cretaceous Period: the early Albian (around 113-107 million years ago) and the early Cenomanian (approximately 100-96 million years ago).

It has been revealed that researchers used powdered fossil material to measure carbon isotope signatures from both periods. They also determined the latitudes where the animals had lived to investigate whether geography influenced the results.

A clear pattern emerged. Fossils from coastal environments consistently contained higher δ13C values than those from the inland formation. Remarkably, the coastal signatures remained similar across different locations, regardless of latitude or geological age.

These findings provide the first evidence of marine subsidization in prehistoric ecosystems, indicating that nutrients originating in the ocean were entering food chains on land millions of years ago.

Seaweed May Have Been on the Dinosaur Menu.

The researchers next considered what ocean food source could explain the widespread chemical signatures.

It has been revealed that "Coastal-dwelling organisms must have eaten some kind of organic matter from the ocean, or prey that had done so. This pattern is shared from fish to megaherbivores and indicates that the extra carbon source must have been low in the food-chain to affect both aquatic and terrestrial animals," Forster explained.

According to recent reports, for the same chemical pattern to appear in such a wide variety of animals, the marine food source would likely have entered the food chain near its base. It also needed to be something that existed along coastlines but was absent farther inland, while remaining available for millions of years.

Seaweed emerged as the most likely explanation.

Recent findings suggest that "Few organisms meet these criteria besides marine macroalgae or macrophytes - seaweeds," noted Forster. "Given the almost ubiquitous behavior of large coastal herbivores today to supplement their diet with seaweeds, it's likely that most of the sampled herbivorous dinosaurs were no different.".

Modern plant-eating animals living near coastlines often consume seaweed to supplement their diets. The fossil evidence suggests that many herbivorous dinosaurs may have behaved similarly, with marine nutrients also passing to other animals through the food chain.

Not Every Dinosaur Had a Taste for the Sea.

Despite the widespread evidence of marine nutrients in coastal food webs, the researchers found that not every dinosaur took advantage of these resources.

One notable exception was Tenontosaurus tilletti, a large plant-eating dinosaur whose fossils have been discovered at numerous locations dating to the Cretaceous Period.

Its tooth enamel contained δ13C values comparable to those of modern animals that feed on plants growing on land. This suggests that Tenontosaurus tilletti did not rely on marine food sources, even though other dinosaurs apparently did.

According to recent reports, the difference also strengthens the researchers' interpretation of the fossil evidence. If geological processes occurring after death had altered the carbon signatures in dinosaur teeth, the same unusual values would be expected more broadly. Instead, the variation between species suggests that the elevated readings reflect genuine differences in diet.

An Ancient Connection Between Land and Ocean.

Although the findings provide strong evidence that marine resources supported the coastal ecosystems examined, vital questions remain.

Sources indicate that the available fossils do not include specimens from polar or equatorial regions during the early Albian and early Cenomanian. As a result, scientists cannot yet determine how widespread this feeding behavior was across different latitudes.

Additional studies will also be needed to establish whether similar relationships existed during other geological periods, including the earlier Jurassic Period and the later early Cenozoic Era.

Beyond revealing a surprising possibility about what dinosaurs ate, the discovery highlights how closely life on land has been connected to the ocean throughout Earth's history.

It has been revealed that "Our study emphasizes the connections between terrestrial and marine ecosystems," concluded Forster. "They are deeply intertwined and have been for hundreds of millions of years. It highlights the importance of environmental linkages across time and space and protecting them where they exist today.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend.

Recent findings suggest that that failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites. ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage, and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further.

It has been revealed that "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an enhancement today (Nov. 18).

This is good news for Blue Origin, Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's Upcoming Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own problems at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28, and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.).

It has been revealed that ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's patch.

Recent findings suggest that vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which rolled out in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit.

In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance.

Recent findings suggest that sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure.

According to recent reports, vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB problem. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

Mikel Arteta states his Arsenal players have been warned against inadvertently leaking team news via Fantasy Premier League.

The intervention comes after Christos Tzolis selected and captained himself in his Fantasy Premier League (FPL) team before Arsenal's match against Liverpool on 1 November, after he had missed a month through injury.

The Gunners manager picked the winger in Arsenal's starting XI at Anfield in what was his first appearance since Greece's Nations League draw with the Netherlands on 1 October.

Before Saturday's match at Newcastle, Arteta said he had to speak to his squad, and those close to the club, about their FPL selections.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," he stated.

"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.

According to recent reports, "This is the kind of thing that is happening in our society right now. It's something upcoming. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.

"Obviously, confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We'll take measures to make sure it doesn't happen.".

The Spaniard also stated his players are restricted from selecting themselves in their FPL line-ups.

In October, a number of FPL teams connected to staff and players at Chelsea removed striker Joao Pedro from their teams, hinting the Brazilian had sustained an injury.

Recent findings suggest that but on Sunday, Greene was featured on CBS’ “60 Minutes” in an interview the long-running show promoted on Twitter with the tease: “Republican Rep. It's time for Marjorie Taylor Greene to go.

According to recent reports, in the segment that aired Sunday night, Stahl noted the congresswoman had moved from the fringe to the GOP’s front row in two years despite a “sharp tongue” and “some pretty radical views” as well as “over the top” comments such as “the Democrats are a party of pedophiles.” Stahl also referred to video of Greene chasing a Parkland, Florida, school shooting survivor, still maintaining that the 2020 election was stolen and failing to criticize Trump over spending. (The interview was conducted before news of his indictment.).

But Stahl didn’t mention Greene spoke at a white nationalist event a year ago while a member of Congress or her extreme anti-Muslim views and her defense of January 6 rioters.

According to recent reports, criticism of CBS for amplifying Greene has been swift and well-deserved even before the program aired. Former GOP Rep. Adam Kinzinger of Illinois tweeted beforehand: “Wow. Insane that 60 min would do this.” (Kinzinger is a CNN senior political commentator.).

Journalist Molly Jong-Fast also slammed “60 Minutes” with the tweet: “Attention is currency and 60 minutes is spending its currency on the Jewish space lasers woman.” (Jong-Fast was apparently referring to Greene’s past claim that a massive California wildfire was started by “a laser” beamed from space controlled by a prominent Jewish banking family.).

David Hogg, who survived the 2018 horrific school shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland and has since become an activist against gun violence, responded, “I look forward to your questions about why she thinks school shootings are fake and why she’s supported QAnon.”.

And while we may disagree on some complications, I respect her greatly.”.

Sources indicate that now, it is true that “60 Minutes” over its 50-plus-year history has featured what the show has dubbed “controversial” guests. These include a 2000 interview with Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh, whose 1995 terrorist attack left 168 dead, including 19 children. And the show did a 1979 interview with Iran’s Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

According to recent reports, perhaps “60 Minutes” views Greene — who has repeatedly downplayed and even defended the January 6, 2021, attack plus called for the GOP to become the party of “Christian nationalism” — in the vein of its long list of controversial guests. (CBS had not responded to a request from CNN for comment at time of publishing.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During talks on ending the war in Ukraine, Russian representatives in Abu Dhabi presented a document containing far-reaching demands, The Upcoming York Times reports.

Dated November 10, the document reportedly calls not only for an end to Western arms deliveries to Ukraine but also for NATO to withdraw its troops and bases and move them back to where they were in 1997.

It has been revealed that the year 1997 refers to the NATO alliance before its first eastward expansion, according to the Kremlin. At the time, NATO had 16 members. Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary had already been invited to join but did not formally become members of the defense alliance until two years later. In the following years, more countries in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe joined, followed most recently by countries in Scandinavia. Today, NATO has 32 member states in Europe and North America.

According to the report, Russia is not explicitly demanding that Central and Eastern European countries leave, but rather that the NATO alliance end its military presence in those countries.

According to recent reports, A withdrawal of NATO troops and bases from member states that joined the alliance after 1997 would significantly weaken their defense capabilities. For example, since 2004, NATO allies, including Germany, have taken turns policing the airspace over Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

According to recent reports, because the Baltic states do not have fighter jets of their own for independent air policing, NATO provides the capability. Since 2026, the mission has been part of a broader air defense presence. The planned deployment of the German Lithuania Brigade, which is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2027, would also have to be halted.

In Romania, meanwhile, the Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base near Constanța on the Black Sea is currently being expanded. Once completed, it is set to become Europe's largest NATO air base by area — even larger than Ramstein in Germany.

Recent findings suggest that "Under no circumstances will we allow anyone to establish new security rules for this part of the world over the heads of Poland and Europe," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told TVP World. His Bulgarian counterpart, Rumen Radev, called a NATO withdrawal "unthinkable and unrealistic." No country should be forced by external pressure to reverse its decision on which alliance to join.

Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal also rejected any Russian say in changes to Europe's security order: "We have nothing to discuss with Russia about Europe's security order; it is working well.".

The strong rejection from the capitals of NATO's eastern members, however, masks fears along the alliance's eastern flank that a deal between Washington and Moscow could turn their security into a bargaining chip.

Industry observers note that in the event of an armed attack on a NATO member, the other alliance members are obligated under Article 5 to come to its aid. Each member decides for itself what measures it considers necessary, which may include the use of military force.

In a recent development, for the mutual defense commitment to deter a potential aggressor, that country must believe NATO can intervene militarily rapidly and effectively in a crisis. The deployment of allied troops along the eastern flank serves precisely this purpose. A withdrawal would make defense more difficult and could lead Russia to believe that an attack on NATO territory would involve fewer risks for Moscow.

Recent findings suggest that as part of their security framework, European countries have agreed that states are free to decide which alliances they wish to join. NATO points to Article 10 of its founding treaty, which enshrines its open-door policy for European countries. The 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act also explicitly stated that neither side had the right to veto the other's decisions.

Back in November 1990, the participating states of the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe (CSCE), including the Soviet Union, had already agreed in the Charter of Paris to respect each country's freedom to choose its own security arrangements.

During the negotiations surrounding German reunification, then-US Secretary of State James Baker and German Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher used language that suggested putting limits on NATO's eastward expansion.

Recent findings suggest that their remarks came during discussions about unified Germany's membership in NATO and the possible deployment of NATO forces on the territory of the former East Germany. However, no written, legally binding general promise was ever agreed that NATO would never expand to include other former Warsaw Pact countries.

Recent findings suggest that in the 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act, both sides declared that they no longer considered each other adversaries. NATO stated that, under the security conditions prevailing at the time and in the foreseeable future, it intended to ensure its collective defense through reinforcement rather than the additional permanent stationing of "substantial combat forces." The agreement explicitly gave Moscow no veto over NATO decisions.

In the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, Russia, the United States and the United Kingdom reaffirmed their commitment to respect Ukraine's independence and existing borders and to refrain from the use of force. These assurances were linked to Ukraine's decision to give up its nuclear weapons. However, the memorandum did not oblige the United States or the United Kingdom to defend Ukraine militarily in the event of an attack. NATO membership was not addressed at the time.

Just over two months before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the Kremlin presented two draft treaties to the United States and NATO. In them, Russia demanded an end to further NATO enlargement. The draft agreement with NATO also proposed that Russia and NATO members that had already joined the alliance as of May 27, 1997, refrain from deploying additional troops or weapons on the territory of other European countries beyond the levels stationed there on that date.

In a recent development, security guarantees for the postwar period and a future security framework for Europe were also on the agenda in Abu Dhabi. Negotiating NATO troop deployments and alliance enlargement alongside an end to the war in Ukraine would give Moscow additional leverage. Russia has long maintained that the "root causes" of the war must be addressed. The Kremlin includes NATO enlargement and the alliance's military presence in Eastern Europe among those causes.

So far, no significant Western player has expressed willingness to accept Russia's demands in Abu Dhabi. On the contrary, former Polish intelligence coordinator Stanislaw Zaryn viewed the talks as an attempt to buy time and weaken the West ahead of another confrontation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that for Pochettino, it was emotional.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Argentinian has excelled in man-management – but will need his powers to energise latest squad and impress owners.

In a recent development, mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style. It was March 2022, he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain and the venue was a stunning boutique hotel; the kind that many capitals have but only Paris truly does. Pochettino’s family and friends were there. So were his inner coaching circle, who are basically family. There were lots of people from PSG. And a good time was had by all.

Sources indicate that for Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the newly introduced Manchester United head coach is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.

Pochettino’s PSG players were at the party. There was no need for anything from them. But there were loads from those he had coached at his previous clubs: Espanyol, Southampton and Tottenham. One by one, the faces flashed up; too many to mention. And, of course, there were the jokes about how old he was getting. But the tone was of pure affection; appreciation, too. Some of the players laid it on thick. They could not help it. They know what Pochettino has done for them.

This is what total buy-in looks like and this is how Pochettino gets you when he finds out which buttons to press. It might be a third-choice goalkeeper. Or a global superstar – for example, Kylian Mbappé, who Pochettino had at PSG. There is a story from those days that is worth sharing. Pochettino was due to give an interview and told the TV crew he would get Mbappé along to speak to them as well.

In a recent development, everybody knows this is not how it works, that it would not be possible because Mbappé, well … he has his time and commitments tightly managed. They appreciated the sentiment from Pochettino, though. When the hour came, Pochettino took out his phone and messaged Mbappé. “Come to the media centre.” Five minutes later, there he was. A line from one of the production staff was gold. “Err, we’ve got Kylian Mbappé outside.”.

This kind of thing is not confined to the dim and distant past. Remember when Pochettino left Chelsea in 2024 and the tributes some of the players paid to him on social media? One stood out because it came from Nicolas Jackson, who Pochettino had punished for getting too many silly yellow cards by ordering him to sprint around the training ground, reducing him to a face-in-the-ground mess when it was over. “Love you coach,” Jackson wrote. “Thanks for the advice and support. You’re a true lion and a fighter.”.

It is easy to feel Pochettino has signed up for his biggest fight because it is not only that United have one Premier League win, a place in the relegation zone, no confidence, questionable fitness levels and a trip to Liverpool on Sunday which has the makings of root canal surgery without the anaesthetic.

In a recent development, hanging heavy over everything is the fan fury towards the Glazer family, who have owned the club since 2005. It is obviously not a upcoming thing. The diehards were passionately against them even before the takeover. But we are going through another period where the frustration has spiked and the malevolence can be heard in the chants. It is the insoluble problem, with the efforts of the minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the director of football, Jason Wilcox, making it worse. They have also been targeted by the Stretford End.

Pochettino knows managers do not tend to enter clubs when everything is rosy. There are reasons why the vacancies arise and they are almost always bad. He has told himself this. What he intends to do is what he has always done: create connections, starting with the players; inject his trademark positivity into every pore; build belief.

The Argentinian is obsessed with what he calls energia universal. It is a guiding life force that influences everything, which touches on concepts such as karma and what these days would probably be called manifestation. He once mentioned it helped to explain, for example, why the London-born Harry Kane usually scored for Spurs in London derbies.

Industry observers note that pochettino wants to release the pressure from United’s beleaguered squad and his early messaging has come from his tried and trusted playbook. He will treat each player as a human being, first and foremost, with individual needs. And, if necessary, individually tailored programmes. At Southampton, he put one together for Luke Shaw, then an emerging player. He has been reunited with the left-back at Old Trafford.

Pochettino talked at his media conference on Friday of having had three hours of one-on-one meetings with the players on Thursday; trying to understand what was happening with them on and off the field. Previously, in his opening address to the United fanbase via the club’s in-house channels, he stressed the importance of everybody “connecting together”.

In a recent development, “The responsibility I feel is energy, it’s excitement,” he said. “To connect with the game we need to feel free. The players need to express their talent and we need to create the environment for them to perform. That is the priority.”.

Sources indicate that pochettino has been close to the United job before – most notably in the summer of 2022 when he left PSG. It was either him or Erik ten Hag to take over from the interim Ralf Rangnick, who had declared that United needed “open-heart surgery”. What do they need now?! The club went for Ten Hag.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino was in United’s thoughts when they looked for a successor to Louis van Gaal in May 2016; he had lunch with Sir Alex Ferguson at Scott’s in London that month. It was believed Ferguson was pushing him as a candidate. United appointed José Mourinho. There was also the period after Mourinho’s dismissal in December 2018 and the interim hire of Ole Gunnar Solskjær when Pochettino was tipped to go to Old Trafford. In the end, Solskjær earned the role on a permanent basis.

According to recent reports, why are United turning now to a manager they have previously overlooked? Pochettino is not about to dwell on that because he is in dream-come-true territory. He will love how the United support stand behind their manager, especially in troublesome times. He will love the pageantry and event glamour of Old Trafford. And he will love having Ferguson in the crowd for the matches.

Pochettino first encountered him in January 2013 when, in his second Southampton game, he went to Old Trafford to face Ferguson’s United, who won 2-1. Pochettino has mentioned that this week. And the meal at Scott’s. And how he was at the Camp Nou for Ferguson’s finest hour: the 1999 Champions League final victory against Bayern Munich. Pochettino was an Espanyol player at the time, together with Toni Jiménez, who is part of his coaching staff, and they watched the first half from so-so seats before blagging their way into the directors’ box for the second period.

Industry observers note that when Solskjær scored his iconic late winner, Pochettino and Jiménez celebrated wildly. They were caught up in the moment. It was the first time Pochettino felt a connection to United and he began to pay more attention to them. And Ferguson. Pochettino described him this week as “the best coach in the history of the sport” but it was not a soundbite of convenience. He has always maintained this and remarked so on the record after the lunch at Scott’s.

How can Pochettino position himself in terms of the Glazers and Ratcliffe? The first thing to say is that he does have experience of unpopular and/or difficult owners. At Spurs, Daniel Levy was forever maligned by the fans, and Pochettino had problems with the American ownership at Chelsea. Between times, the Qataris at PSG were not easy. Pochettino worked to build a relationship with Levy, regularly saying nice things about him in the press and famously including him on a staff-bonding trip to Argentina.

It featured white-water rafting and ended with Pochettino having to fish Levy out of the Manso River. A repeat of the adventure with Joel Glazer feels unlikely but Pochettino’s starting point at United has been to stress unity; the need to create chemistry with everyone, including “the directors and the owners”.

And so to Anfield, where Pochettino first managed with Southampton in September 2013 when his team won 1-0. He has not tasted victory in his eight subsequent trips; seven with Spurs, one with Chelsea, the record reveals two draws and six defeats. No United fan expects anything this time but Pochettino considers it a great game to have. He will certainly learn a lot about his players.

#36271. Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns

Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 exceptionally ancient quasars, including two that have set fresh records as the earliest ever observed.
  • Quasars are among the brightest objects in the cosmos.
  • Astronomers have spent decades searching for quasars from the Universe's earliest years because they offer valuable clues about the formation of the first galaxies and supermassive black holes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 exceptionally ancient quasars, including two that have set fresh records as the earliest ever observed. These brilliant galactic centers, powered by enormous black holes, were already radiating as much light as a trillion Suns when the Universe was only 670 million years old, about 5% of its present age.

Quasars are among the brightest objects in the cosmos. They appear during a relatively short period in a galaxy's history when huge quantities of gas and other material spiral toward its central supermassive black hole. This process releases extraordinary amounts of energy, causing the galaxy's core to shine hundreds or even thousands of times more brightly than the rest of the galaxy combined.

Astronomers have spent decades searching for quasars from the Universe's earliest years because they offer valuable clues about the formation of the first galaxies and supermassive black holes. Finding them, however, is extremely challenging. Few galaxies had grown large enough to host such objects at that early stage, and the light reaching us today is incredibly faint. These distant sources can also be difficult to distinguish from stars much closer to Earth.

It has been revealed that launched in 2023, Euclid is transforming that search. Its ability to survey enormous regions of the sky and detect faint objects has already produced an unprecedented collection of 31 quasars from the early Universe, including some dating back to when the cosmos was just 5% of its current age.

Industry observers note that "These early quasars date back to the Universe's infancy," indicates Daming Yang of Leiden University in the Netherlands, lead author of the Euclid discovery paper. "By finding and studying them, we can better understand how these enormous systems formed and grew so promptly - one of the greatest mysteries in astrophysics.".

Euclid Reveals a Hidden Population of Ancient Quasars.

It has been revealed that until now, astronomers had identified only a small fraction of the quasars that existed during the Universe's earliest period. Most known examples were exceptionally luminous objects that stood out because they were easier to detect. This limited sample made it difficult to understand the broader population and how these powerful systems developed.

Sources indicate that euclid is changing that picture by identifying not only the brightest quasars but also much fainter examples that previous searches struggled to find. Its discoveries are providing scientists with a far more representative view of the ancient quasar population, opening the door to more detailed studies of these early cosmic objects.

"Euclid is a true game-changer," adds Daming. "Before, we could only find a handful of the very brightest ancient quasars, but Euclid lets us search far more efficiently across huge areas of sky to capture much fainter light. It's a unique tool for quasar hunting.".

Among the 31 newly identified quasars, 12 have a redshift of 7 or greater. Redshift describes how light is stretched as the Universe expands and helps astronomers determine how far away an object is and how far back in cosmic history its light originated. A redshift of at least 7 places these quasars within the Universe's first 770 million years.

Two Record-Breaking Quasars From Cosmic Dawn.

Two objects stand out as particularly extraordinary. The most ancient, EUCL J172902.75+641018.1, has a redshift of 7.77, while EUCL J125308.55+705432.3 has a redshift of 7.69. Both are located just over 13 billion light-years from Earth and were already shining within the first 670 million years of cosmic history.

These discoveries establish new records for the earliest known quasars. The previous record belonged to an object discovered in 2021, which has a redshift of 7.64.

"This finding more than doubles the number of quasars we know of that are so ancient," claims Antonio La Marca, an ESA Research Fellow in the Euclid team.

In a recent development, the pace of discovery is especially remarkable. Astronomers needed more than a decade to identify roughly the first 10 quasars with redshifts of 7 or higher. Euclid has already surpassed that number in just one year, demonstrating how dramatically the telescope is accelerating research into the early Universe.

Sources indicate that "The Euclid team has taken a true 'census' of quasars at the dawn of the Universe for the first time," adds Antonio. "It's a big step towards understanding these fascinating objects on a more fundamental level.".

Ancient Black Holes Reveal Clues About the First Galaxies.

One of the newly discovered objects is already offering additional insight into conditions during the Universe's infancy. Silvia Belladitta and colleagues recently conducted a more detailed investigation of the second most ancient quasar identified by Daming and his team.

Sources indicate that their observations revealed that the quasar sits inside a galaxy filled with gas and dust where latest stars are forming at a tremendous rate. This provides an important glimpse of the environment surrounding an early supermassive black hole and could help researchers understand how the first massive galaxies evolved alongside the black holes at their centers.

Industry observers note that these quasars also belong to a transformative chapter in cosmic history known as the epoch of reionization. During this period, the Universe emerged from a cold, dark state (the 'dark ages') as increasingly energetic radiation heated the surrounding gas and ionized it (split apart by energetic light). This fundamental transition helped establish the conditions that shaped the Universe we observe today.

In a recent development, "Ancient quasars are rare discoveries. They're interesting in themselves, but also time machines that enable us to explore the early Universe and understand how the first generation of galaxies came to be," notes ESA Euclid Project Scientist Valeria Pettorino.

How Euclid Is Transforming the Search for Cosmic Giants.

It has been revealed that euclid's success comes from a powerful combination of capabilities. The telescope can examine enormous portions of the sky while collecting detailed images and detecting faint infrared light from extremely distant objects. Together, these features make it exceptionally effective at finding rare sources that earlier surveys could easily miss.

In a recent development, "Euclid's capabilities are unrivaled. The telescope combines a large area, depth, sharp imaging, and unique space-based infrared vision in a way that lets us pick out rare, extremely distant objects far more efficiently than before.

"And it's not just the telescope: the data processing is only possible thanks to thousands of Euclid Consortium scientists and engineers working together to deliver scientific discoveries, sifting through enormous datasets to identify rare, distant quasars that we can study further using telescopes on the ground.".

All 31 quasars were identified using observations from the Euclid Wide Survey, an ambitious project that will eventually examine more than one-third of the entire sky.

Although Euclid's primary mission is to investigate the dark Universe, its observations are revealing much more. By studying billions of galaxies, the telescope is helping astronomers investigate the Universe's composition, history, evolution, and vast cosmic structure. At the same time, its sweeping survey is uncovering rare ancient quasars that offer a remarkable opportunity to explore how the first galaxies and giant black holes emerged.

As Euclid continues mapping the cosmos, astronomers expect its growing collection of distant quasars to provide new clues about one of astrophysics' most enduring questions: how supermassive black holes became so enormous in such a remarkably short time after the Major Bang.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada (left) with director of football Jason Wilcox.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada notes some of the criticism aimed at the club's hierarchy has "crossed a line".

In a rare interview to Sky Sports as head coach Mauricio Pochettino prepares for his first game in charge, at Liverpool on Sunday, Berrada said he "understood" the frustration of supporters at United being 18th in the Premier League. He also said some of the criticism was "fair".

Industry observers note that "Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and scrutiny we're going to get," he said. "We accept it. Some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line.

"We do live in this world of social media, where people like to generate negative stories about the club because it drives more engagement, and it drives more general noise and activity around the club. But we park that.".

United's director of football Jason Wilcox has been singled out by supporters at recent games. There have also been social media calls for both Wilcox and Berrada to lose their jobs.

In addition, songs are now sung regularly calling for minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to leave, while opposition to the Glazer family has remained intense since their leveraged buyout in 2005 saddled debt on to the club that now exceeds Â£1bn.

Cost of Man Utd hiring and firing managers nears Â£100m.

Andrey Santos has started four Premier League games for Manchester United since his Â£50m summer move from Chelsea.

Wilcox, in particular, has been blamed for what is perceived to have been poor summer recruitment. After the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid in September, defender Lisandro Martinez mentioned he "expected more from the technical director".

Ousted boss Michael Carrick felt he was let down by a transfer strategy that targeted midfield, while not addressing issues at left-back and in attack - which has been compounded by injuries to Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko.

According to recent reports, carrick wanted to target Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes, but United backed off when Nottingham Forest and West Ham's demands went higher than they wanted to pay. Anderson eventually joined Manchester City for Â£116m, with Fernandes moving to Tottenham for Â£85m.

Instead, United paid a combined Â£118m for Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos, who have started seven Premier League games between then, and triggered Youri Tielemans' Â£35m release clause at Aston Villa. Tielemans scored his first United goal in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on 8 November and has one assist.

However, Berrada has defended United's transfer business, saying: "When we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we're receiving a lot of criticism for it, but we're actually happy with the players we bought.

"We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, and Karl Darlow - and let's not forget that we've also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona - these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

Recent findings suggest that "We went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play and we've said consistently in the last few years we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players, for the right value at the right time - in terms of what the squad needs.

Recent findings suggest that "When we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don't want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it. So, could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players at the right value.

"There's no point in us spending Â£40m, Â£50m for players we're not convinced are going to add value to the team.".

When he spoke to the wider media for the first time, 30 minutes before Berrada's interview was aired, Pochettino said he hoped to have a say in all areas of the playing side, even though his official title is head coach.

"I know that, being a head coach, I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday," he noted. "I'm going to pick the starting 11 and I'm going to make the changes.

"Of course, in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad.".

Pochettino on his arrival at Man Utd.

Berrada said there had been little option other than to dismiss Carrick given United's plight and the team had "dropped off in many areas".

Pochettino has spoken individually to virtually every player to get an understanding of what the challenges are.

He mentioned he was wary of reading too much into data that shows United's players have not been running enough, arguing "if you don't put context on the data, it's very dangerous to talk".

The 54-year-old also mentioned that, despite talking extensively about culture in his first in-house interview on Thursday, it could take 10 years to build one.

"The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear," he stated. "It's a historic club, one of the best in the world. It's difficult to find another club the size of Manchester United.

According to recent reports, "The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear. It needs to be in a different place than we are now.".

Pochettino did confirm Bruno Fernandes will remain as skipper for the trip to Liverpool.

Fernandes has struggled for form and, with the 32-year-old's contract due to expire in the summer, there has been no breakthrough in negotiations over an extension.

United do have the option to trigger an additional year on the Portugal playmaker's present deal but, given the massive dip from the levels that earned him all last season's major player of the year awards, there are some who wonder whether a clean break might be best.

Pochettino preferred to deflect the wider aspect of Fernandes' future and concentrate on the immediate.

"Bruno is our captain and he's a very notable player," he stated.

"I think we will have time after to talk about the [other] things that you are asking me.".

Nick Cannon is reaching out to his fans.

The Masked Singer host shared that he’s in the hospital amid his ongoing battle with the autoimmune disease Lupus, asking his fans to keep him in their thoughts.

“This [world emoji] can definitely take a lot out of you!” Cannon posted to Instagram Nov. 20, alongside a photo of himself wearing a mask in a hospital bed. “Pray for me y’all.”.

The 46-year-old captioned the photo, “#LupusWarrior.”.

And certainly Cannon has never shied away from being candid about his struggles with Lupus after his 2012 diagnosis, especially when it comes to how he does his best to manage the disease.

Recent findings suggest that “When I got diagnosed… [it felt] so life-altering,” the Wild ’n Out host admitted to Us Weekly in September. “Now, it becomes like, ‘So what?’ It’s a part of my life. It keeps me in check. I have to eat correctly, get rest and exercise twice a day.”.

According to recent reports, in fact, Cannon felt like the diagnosis was almost “a blessing disguise,” adding that most people his age “aren’t up at 4 a.m. to go to the gym.”.

“I work out to stay alive,” he added. “It’s a challenge, but I’m built for it.”.

And of course, Cannon wants to make sure he’s in top shape to help care for his kids, including 15-year-old twins Moroccan and Monroe with ex-wife Mariah Carey; Golden Sagon, 9, Powerful Queen, 5, and Rise Messiah, 4, with Brittany Bell; 5-year-old twins Zion Mixolydian and Zillion Heir as well as Beautiful Zeppelin, 3, with Abby De La Rosa; Legendary Love, 4, with Bre Tiesi; and Onyx Ice, 4, with LaNisha Cole.

He is also father to son Zen—who tragically died at 5 months old in 2021 after being diagnosed with brain cancer—as well as daughter Halo Marie, 3, with Alyssa Scott.

And when he looks back on his original diagnosis, there’s one person who he believes helped him survive during the first few months: Mariah Carey.

"She was my rock," he shared on The Diary Of A CEO podcast in 2023. "She went hard. To be honest, I probably wouldn't be alive if it wasn't for how hard she went with the doctors, with me, my stubbornness.".

"She was the perfect helpmate," he added. "The perfect matriarch. The perfect mom. The perfect wife in those scenarios, because granted she's who she is and dealing with all the pressures of being Mariah Carey, but then being loving enough to take on all my stuff.".

The Grammy winner’s dedication didn’t come as a surprise to the Drumline star, as he noted, "That's what you do when you find a helpmate. When you find someone you're in matrimony with, you go hard for them.".

For a look at more stars who have shared their own difficult health scares, keep reading.

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better.".

According to recent reports, "Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much.".

The actress said she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant.".

And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors said they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. Jamie Foxx's Brain Bleed & Stroke.

Industry observers note that emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress mentioned on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of issues and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Major Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that.".

Bayern Munich confirm Harry Kane ‘out for next few months’ with ankle injury

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (807 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • England forward injured in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne.
  • Club statement confirms ‘tear of ligament in left ankle’.
  • Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England forward injured in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne.

Club statement confirms ‘tear of ligament in left ankle’.

Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.

Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted and the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, noted that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.

In a recent development, A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”.

Sources indicate that the Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired the visitors ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half, and Mentioned El Mala missed an excellent late chance to earn Cologne’s first win at Bayern since 2009.

The 33-year-old may face a race to be fit for the Nations League quarter-finals, the first leg of which takes place in Norway on 27 March – just over four months away. The Bayern sporting director, Max Eberl, stated on Friday that club doctors were “discussing whether or not to recommend surgery” for Kane’s injury.

Part of Kane’s recovery period will come during the Bundesliga’s winter break from 20 December to 8 January. He will, however, miss Champions League games away to Lille next week and at home to Slavia Prague next month, as well as the January trip to Manchester United and the league phase finale at home to Real Betis.

Kane’s setback adds to an extensive Bayern injury list, with Olise also going off during Friday’s game with a foot contusion. Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and Manuel Neuer were already unavailable, leaving Kompany short of options for a busy month of fixtures.

In a recent development, kompany returned from his own month-long absence for Friday’s game with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on a training pitch in October. The Belgian was taken to hospital for meningeal irritation treatment after his collapse, and has been recovering at home.

Recent findings suggest that “I think this result was fair and Cologne deserved the point,” Kompany said after the game. “We have other worries now, I have to honestly say. We will all try together to make something strong out of this situation. FC Bayern does that time and again, and that’s what we want to do now too.”.

Cologne took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone when Moore started and finished an excellent break. The teenage winger pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala, whose no-look backheel pass allowed Moore to round keeper Jonas Urbig before sliding the ball home.

Kane was then brought down in the Cologne box from behind by Schmied, who got the ball first but clattered into Kane’s left leg in his follow-through. Kane’s penalty appeals were waved away, but he was left visibly limping and received treatment on his ankle before being replaced by Tom Bischof on the 20-minute mark.

It has been revealed that the hosts levelled 17 minutes later when full-back Brown sliced a low shot into the bottom-right corner, but suffered another blow just before the break when Olise went down. The France star did not return for the second half and was seen leaving the stadium shortly after on crutches – but it appears unlikely he will miss a significant amount of time.

Recent findings suggest that just before the hour mark, El Mala and Maina forced a spectacular double save from Urbig. El Mala, recently called up by Germany, then had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig – but he cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post.

Now a point behind Bayern, Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first place if they win at bottom club Mönchengladbach on Saturday. Freiburg can also move level on points with Bayern if they can defeat promoted Elversberg.

This month Kane signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029, which is reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.

Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has scored an incredible 156 goals in 163 appearances, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the company's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire. So they did the only thing they could think to do—they built an expansive alternate-universe internet that they completely control.

“Web-use” agents need to be familiar with the open internet, how to navigate real websites and platforms, and how to be hardened against web attacks. So training them in limited test environments is only so effective. Plus, models can develop what's known as “eval awareness,” where they behave differently because they have determined that they are in a test or simulation. On the other hand, setting unrefined agents loose on the open internet is a bad idea. That’s where the alternate-universe internet comes in.

According to recent reports, the “Mirror Dimension,” which Google is detailing in a blog post today for the first time, is a sweeping and diverse but isolated web ecosystem that the Chrome team entirely controls. It includes a vast array of websites and platforms—including social media sites, shopping, and bank dashboards—that are built with all the components and attributes of real websites. Browsing assistant agents must interact with the sites and complete tasks in Chrome the way they would on the real internet. And they face resilience tests as they go, like hidden prompt-injection attacks, to test their defenses.

In a recent development, “Agents are not programmed, so you can’t predict every possible thing an agent might see; the exploration space that we have to address is huge, and the web is hostile,” notes Charles Qian, a software engineer on the Chrome AI security team. “Any user can ask any prompt on any website, so we really need to explore that space as thoroughly as we can. And we’ve seen the agent start to develop a mature sense of judgment when it comes to knowing what information is actually needed for a task and when to punt back to the user for a confirmation.”.

According to recent reports, building out and populating the Mirror Dimension was a challenge in itself, because it needed to be vast and varied enough to represent the scale of the real web while being developed swiftly. To construct it, the Chrome team gathered armies of website and web app development agents guided by a purpose-built AI harness to quickly create realistic web services and data flows—down to details like entering promo codes on a shopping site or populating social media pages.

Even though the entire environment is controlled by Google, Chrome is built with so many user protections and validity checks that, in order to allow the agents to use real Chrome (which is crucial for accurate training), the researchers essentially had to hack the browser and take elaborate steps like making forged web certificates for validity checks so the agents could have a normal experience. The team emphasizes, though, that none of these attacks would be possible against regular Chrome users on the open internet. They were all facilitated by the god-mode-type access and privilege the team inherently has because they control the entire environment and network.

The researchers say that while the browsing assistant agents they have been testing are benign and do not have cyber capabilities, their goal is to make the Mirror Dimension available to teams across Google so more researchers have access to the safe and controlled environment for testing.

Sources indicate that “We’re sharing this approach so other teams both internally and externally think about doing it this way,” states Doug Turner, Google’s director of engineering. “This is the first step; there’s going to be continued investment in this approach to train models. And I would imagine as they become more sophisticated, we’ll have to continue working on this environment to make it more and more realistic.”.

Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
